description.value: The study tested whether medial orbitofrontal cortex gray matter volume is reduced in abstinent substance-dependent individuals compared with control subjects and examined relationships between medial OFC gray matter, decision-making behavior, and substance-dependence symptoms.

design.value: A cross-sectional case-control structural MRI study of 19 substance-dependent individuals after prolonged abstinence and 20 control subjects, using voxel-based morphometry with whole-brain and medial OFC region-of-interest analyses, together with behavioral and correlational analyses.

name.value: International Consortium for Brain Mapping (ICBM) tissue probability maps
Composite International Diagnostic Interview Substance Abuse Module (CIDI-SAM)

description.value: A computerized structured interview for drug dependence; for each drug, symptom count and date of last use were recorded. The symptom count comprised 11 symptoms, from 7 dependence and 4 abuse symptoms.
A modification of the IGT adapted for a functional MRI experiment, with 80 trials in which subjects chose “Play or Pass”; choices to play “bad” decks were totaled over early and late time blocks.
IQ was measured using the two-subtest version, administering the Vocabulary and Matrix Reasoning subtests.

source_definition.value: Total gray matter volume; the effects of total GM volume were removed to allow inferences about regional differences in GM volume.
IQ measured with the two-subtest Wechsler Abbreviated Scale of Intelligence.
The two time blocks, early and late trials.
The group × time interaction in selection of bad decks.
Gender, analyzed in a 2 × 2 gender by group ANOVA.
GM volume obtained from the voxel corresponding to the global maxima of the group difference model that localized to medial OFC (−5, 53, −5, Montreal Neurological Institute).
The number of times an individual chose to play “bad” decks on early compared with late trials was totaled; the hypothesis was that higher GM would correlate with greater avoidance of “bad” cards.
For each drug, CIDI-SAM generated a symptom count, 11 total from 7 dependence and 4 abuse symptoms.
Duration of abstinence from the substances; average abstinence from cocaine, alcohol, and amphetamine was 4.7, 3.2, and 2.4 years, respectively.

description.value: 20 control subjects (14 women/6 men, 33 years old, SD 11 years).

inclusion_criteria.value: No diagnosis of substance abuse or dependence.

education_summary.value: There were differences in education between the groups.

description.value: 19 SDI (9 women/10 men, 35 years old, SD 7 years) who were dependent on one or more illicit substances and were recruited from the University of Colorado School of Medicine Addiction Research and Treatment Service (ARTS), a long-term residential treatment service.

inclusion_criteria.value: Dependence on one or more illicit substances, with DSM-IV criteria.

recruitment_method.value: Recruited from the University of Colorado School of Medicine Addiction Research and Treatment Service (ARTS), a long-term residential treatment service.

medical_condition.value: Dependence on one or more illicit substances

diagnostic_instrument.value: computerized Composite International Diagnostic Interview Substance Abuse Module (CIDI-SAM)

clinical_characteristics.value: The SDI were dependent on two or more substances, most often cocaine, amphetamine, and alcohol, with mean duration of abstinence 4.7, 2.4, and 3.2 years, respectively. Average abstinence from cocaine, alcohol, and amphetamine was 4.7, 3.2, and 2.4 years, respectively. A minimum 2-month treatment compliance was required before participation; the SDI underwent frequent, observed urine drug tests.

education_summary.value: There were differences in education between the groups.

task_description.value: A modification of the IGT adapted for a functional magnetic resonance imaging experiment that simulates uncertainty and reward in real-life decision-making. There were 80 trials for which the subject chose “Play or Pass”; trials were divided into early and late time blocks.

stimuli.value: “Bad” decks in a modified gambling task, representing risky choices with substantial negative consequences.

task_performance_measures.value: The number of times an individual chose to play “bad” decks on early compared with late trials was totaled.

instrument.value: 3-T whole body MR scanner (General Electric, Milwaukee, Wisconsin) with a standard quadrature head coil

description.value: A high-resolution three-dimensional T1-weighted spoiled gradient echo (SPGR)-IR sequence was acquired with repetition time = 45 ms, echo time = 20 ms, flip angle = 45°, 256 2 matrix, 240 mm 2 field-of-view, 0.9 × 0.9 mm 2 in-plane resolution, 1.7-mm thick slice, and coronal plane. Scan time was 9 min 24 sec.

The VBM in SPM5 combines tissue segmentation, bias correction, and spatial normalization into a unified model. Hidden Markov Random Fields were applied to improve the accuracy of tissue segmentation; individual brains were normalized to ICBM tissue probability maps and smoothed with a 12-mm full-width-at-half-maximal Gaussian kernel, resulting in a final smoothing of 14 × 15 × 14 mm 3.

steps.value: Tissue segmentation, bias correction, and spatial normalization were combined into a unified model.
Hidden Markov Random Fields were applied to improve accuracy of tissue segmentation, using medium HMRF .3.
Individual brains were normalized to tissue probability maps provided by International Consortium for Brain Mapping (ICBM).
A 12-mm full-width-at-half-maximal Gaussian kernel was applied, resulting in final smoothing of 14 × 15 × 14 mm 3.

model_settings.value: At the second level, whole brain data were modeled across the groups with total GM volume and age as covariates. An absolute threshold mask of .1 was used. Statistical maps were set at a cluster-level threshold of p < .05, corrected for multiple comparisons with family-wise error (FWE), and a voxel-level threshold of p < .005. A nonisotropic smoothness correction was applied.
A region-of-interest analysis of right and left medial OFC was implemented with the Automated anatomic labeling (AAL) ROI library within Marsbar SPM toolbox.
Repeated measures ANOVA with IQ, education, and age as covariates, analyzing for effects of group × time interaction.
Partial correlation between medial OFC GM volume and behavioral data, adjusted for IQ, education, and total GM; considered significant at p < .05, one-tailed.
Partial correlation between symptom count and medial OFC GM volume, adjusted for total GM, IQ, and age.

A 2 × 2 (gender, group) ANOVA with covariates of age and total GM and multiple comparison correction, evaluating main effects of gender and gender × group interactions on GM volume and decision-making behavior.
The authors subsequently analyzed whether OFC GM correlated with abstinence; no relationship between abstinence and morphology was found.

description.value: One of the two choices available on each gambling-task trial.

The early time block of gambling-task trials.
The late time block of gambling-task trials.
Risky decks whose selection was used to assess decision-making behavior; the number of times an individual chose to play “bad” decks was totaled.

model_representation_notes.value: The ANCOVA adjusted for known confounds of age and global GM; an absolute threshold mask of .1 and nonisotropic smoothness correction were also applied.

interpretations.value: There was significantly more GM specifically in bilateral medial OFC in control subjects compared with SDI.
